description: A security engineering manager must approve the production rollout policy for a critical authentication-gateway patch, including rollout sequencing, customer exceptions, audit evidence, and follow-up commitments, after the standard cross-functional review.

shared_context.S1: A critical patch for the production authentication gateway is available and the current rollout proposal targets all production regions after a 10 percent canary.
shared_context.S2: The standard proposal starts the canary at 02:00 UTC, uses the previous gateway image for rollback, and records ordinary deployment logs.
shared_context.S3: Rina owns the final approval for the production rollout policy.
shared_context.S4: The change-control checklist requires review from platform engineering, customer operations, and compliance before production approval.
shared_context.S5: Before finalizing a change-control decision, the team routinely states operational constraints, discusses how the plan will incorporate them, and the final approver records the resulting policy.
shared_context.S6: For consistency in the change record, whenever a compatibility bridge is included in the rollout, the rollout_mode decision is recorded with the exact phrase "compatibility bridge".

PF1.text: While testing the patch against the service inventory this afternoon, Mateo confirmed that exactly 18 legacy services cannot restart safely until a compatibility bridge has run for 6 hours; he has not updated the rollout proposal because the test finished after the planning meeting.

PF2.text: Leah confirmed from customer maintenance calendars this morning that exactly two customers, Northstar and BluePeak, have blackout windows from 00:00 to 06:00 UTC; their gateway instances must be deferred until 06:00 UTC and both customers must receive direct notices, but she has not added the exception to the change record yet.

PF3.text: Owen confirmed during a compliance evidence review today that this patch requires a signed deployment manifest and immutable retention of its rollout evidence for exactly 180 days; he has not filed the evidence requirement because the security finding was only classified this afternoon.

interaction_config.settle_eligibility: Rina may settle once PF1, PF2, and PF3 have been revealed in the transcript and Rina has acknowledged all three findings and proposed a revised plan incorporating them. No formal sign-off statement from each contributor is required.

acceptance_conditions: The rollout must use a staged compatibility mode.
The compatibility bridge must run for exactly 6 hours.
Exactly Northstar and BluePeak must be listed as deferred customers.
The deferred customer rollout must begin at exactly 06:00 UTC.
A signed deployment manifest must be required.
Rollout evidence must be retained immutably for exactly 180 days.
The settlement must include a commitment that Northstar and BluePeak will receive direct customer notices before deployment, or a decisions field indicating direct notices are required.

The settlement must include a commitment that a signed deployment manifest will be produced and immutable rollout evidence retained for 180 days, or a decisions field indicating these evidence requirements are required.
The compatibility constraint, customer blackout constraint, and compliance evidence requirement must each be cited as justification.

content_checks.C1: 'compatibility bridge' in decisions['rollout_mode'] or 'staged' in decisions['rollout_mode'] or 'bridge gate' in decisions['rollout_mode'] or any(c['type'] == 'compatibility_bridge' and c['services'] == 18 and c['hours'] == 6 for c in commitments)
content_checks.C2: any(c['services'] == 18 and c['hours'] == 6 for c in commitments)
content_checks.C7: any(c['type'] == 'direct_customer_notice' and c['customers'] == ['Northstar', 'BluePeak'] for c in commitments) or decisions['customer_notice_required'] == True
content_checks.C8: any(c['type'] == 'deployment_evidence' and c['hours'] == 180 for c in commitments) or decisions['deployment_evidence_required'] == True

decisive_facts.why: The standard canary plan does not specify a compatibility stage or duration; PF1 changes the rollout mode to include a staged compatibility bridge, requires a commitment covering exactly 18 legacy services, and sets its duration to exactly 6 hours.

The standard plan has no customer exceptions or targeted notices; PF2 changes the exception list to exactly Northstar and BluePeak, moves their rollout to exactly 06:00 UTC, and requires direct notices to both customers.
Ordinary deployment logging is insufficient; PF3 changes the policy to require a signed manifest and exactly 180 days of immutable evidence retention, plus a deployment-evidence commitment.
